subject: Single-season, sing-species models - is an alternative approach to insert detection variables wrong?

messages.author: 3d259ef05152b361
messages.subject: Single-season, sing-species models - is an alternative approach to insert detection variables wrong?
parts:
Good afternoon,

I am trying to run a single-species, single-season occupancy model with unmarked.
My detection history comprehends detection information over 13 sites and 25 sampling occasions.
I also have 6 occupancy variables (say they are X1, X2, ... , X6) and 2 detection variables. The two detection variables are Trap Effort (camera-trap nights) and Human Use of Site (number of H. sapiens captures).

I have gone through several tutorials to try to fit the two detection variables in the obsCovs argument of the unmarkedFrameOccu function, but I have come across with some errors such as:
"
Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) :
  At least one element of obsCovs has incorrect number of dimensions.

Error in validObject(.Object) :
  invalid class “unmarkedFrame” object: obsCovData does not have M*obsNum rows.
"

After reading and experimenting a bit, I believe the reason for these errors lies in the fact that Trap Effort (camera-trap nights) and Human Use of Site (number of H. sapiens captures) concern their global (as in, total in the end of the survey) values per site, instead of being two matrixes of values corresponding to each sampling occasion per site. Given this is the case, my question is: is it wrong to add these (non-changeable) detection covariates to the siteCovs argument and then use the occu function in the following manner(?):

unmarkedFrameOccuObject <- umarkedFrameOccu(y = DetectionHistory,
                                            siteCovs = siteCovs, # dataframe with detection and occupancy variables
                                            obsCovs = NULL)

GlobalModel <- occu(~TrapEffort + HumanUseSites
                    ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + X5 + X6,
                    data = unmarkedFrameOccuObject)


(Later, I will use dredge() on GlobalModel)
Sorry if this is a very basic question, just want to make sure I am not running my models in a wrong way.

Thanks!
Regards,
Luís

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Single-season, sing-species models - is an alternative approach to insert detection variables wrong?
parts:
Hi Luis,

Yes, it's fine to use a site covariate within the formula/model for variation in p-- p can vary across sites, across occasions, or across sites*occasions. 

John
